decision: NOT re-pinned here.  Re-pointing a launch authorization to a hash the owner has not named manufactures consent; these are T4 rescue contracts and this is a PMO branch.  The guard is working as designed -- it is reporting that the runtime a T4 authorization covers has changed.
options_for_the_owner: Re-pin the four contracts and re-run their matched confirmation, if the construction prior is intended to be in the T4 runtime too.
Merge the PMO wiring only after those rescues have run, so no authorized T4 launch straddles the change.
Rejected: duplicating the lane into a second module to avoid the pin. Two copies of the construction draw would drift apart, which is a worse failure than a re-pin.

regression_check.impacted_test_closure: 25 test files importing dynamic_program_synthesis, pmo_population_controller or learned_successor_prior
regression_check.reading: The failure sets are identical, so no test that was green went red. The 14 are pre-existing: two are `max_modules` guards that were never updated when MAX_GENERIC_MODULES moved from 3 to 8, and the rest are contract/hash-pin and recovery tests already red at the branch base.

what: Wiring the chemical prior into the PMO construction lane edits `src/compose_v4/control/dynamic_program_synthesis.py`, which several T4 launch contracts pin by file hash in their runtime inputs.  Those contracts will refuse to launch with an input-identity mismatch until they are explicitly re-pinned.
